market_context: U.S. futures are modestly higher, with S&P 500 futures up about 0.2% and Dow futures up about 0.4%, while Nasdaq 100 futures are roughly flat.[1] Tesla is a notable premarket leader after unveiling its redesigned Roadster, while Apple is reportedly up nearly 2% on strong iPhone Duo preorders; technology remains vulnerable to AI-spending and debt concerns.[1][7]

predictions.reasoning: S&P 500 futures indicate an approximately 0.2% higher open, and easing concerns about an October rate move are supporting broad equities.[1][4] Recent weakness in technology may limit the advance, so the expected gain is modest.

Nasdaq 100 futures were approximately flat to slightly negative while AI-spending and AI-debt concerns continue to pressure large-cap technology.[1][2][7] QQQ has already declined 4.0% over five sessions, increasing rebound risk but leaving it relatively exposed if tech weakness resumes.

Tesla rose roughly 3% to 5% premarket after revealing its redesigned Roadster, creating a strong identifiable catalyst.[1][2][6] The sizable premarket move raises the risk of profit-taking, so the target assumes only partial continuation rather than a full 5% gain.

Apple was reported nearly 2% higher before the open after iPhone Duo preorders reportedly sold out shortly after launch.[7] The catalyst is company-specific and may help Apple outperform a mixed technology tape, although early gains could fade.

Large-cap AI exposure remains pressured by renewed concerns over the durability of AI spending and debt-funded infrastructure investment.[1][2][7] Nvidia may receive some support from CEO Jensen Huang's positive comments on CoreWeave, but sector-wide risk argues for a slight decline.
